Starting today, Runna subscribers can access the new "Adapt for Heat" feature, which automatically adjusts pace targets based on local temperature and humidity. Details below.

Runna adds heat-aware training tool

Personal running coach app Runna today announced three updates designed to support users throughout their training cycle, covering everything from training in hot weather to post-race recovery.

Launching today, the new "Adapt for Heat" feature will help users identify cooler running windows and recommend adjusted pace targets based on feels-like temperature, workout duration and specific session content.

"Adapt for Heat" displays an hourly, colour-coded weather forecast so users can quickly identify the best time to run and plan accordingly.

Here's Runna introducing the new feature:

Runna also announced the relaunch of its "Post-Race Recovery Plan" feature. Once a user begins a race plan from 5K to 50K, a recovery plan will be automatically generated. Steph Kessell, Runna's head coach and former Olympian, said these plans are designed by expert coaches to help runners "reduce the risk of wear-and-tear or injury."

Finally, the platform announced a new feature, "Upcoming Plans," set to launch in August. The feature lets users queue up multiple training plans and automatically transition into the next one when a plan ends, further streamlining long-term training.

Here's Runna explaining the benefits of the "Upcoming Plans" feature:

Plan your entire year of training in minutes: Runners can stack races, milestone goals and training blocks for a full overview of the year ahead. Zero admin between plans: No need to rebuild or start over—your preferred training schedule, projected finish time and current fitness carry over automatically when one plan ends and the next begins. Total flexibility, total control: Every plan can be edited, swapped or deleted at any time, so runners stay fully in charge of their experience. Designed for progressive development: Each plan is built by Runna's expert coaches following established training principles, helping runners progress steadily, manage recovery and arrive at the start line ready to perform.
